repairs.before: Aristotle’s long-lived physical errors illustrate how prestige cannot replace observation, making science’s empirical correction mechanism safer than unsupported speculation.
repairs.after: Atkins invokes Aristotle’s largely nonempirical physics, whose errors persisted for millennia, to argue that scientific observation corrects unsupported speculation more reliably than prestige.
